definitions.explanation: Chicken skin as food, especially the yakitori skewer made of it. Grilled long enough to render the fat, it comes out crisp outside and chewy inside, and is a standard cheap item on an izakaya menu.

examples.japanese: {鳥皮|とりかわ}を{二本|にほん}ください。
{鳥皮|とりかわ}はパリパリに{焼|や}いたほうがおいしい。
examples.english: Chicken skin tastes better grilled until it's crispy.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}の{鳥皮|とりかわ}は{脂|あぶら}がよく{落|お}ちていて、{塩|しお}で{食|た}べるのが{一番|いちばん}だ。
examples.english: The skin skewers here have the fat well rendered out, and they're best eaten with just salt.

notes:
Also written {鶏皮|とりかわ}, which is the more precise spelling since {鶏|とり} means chicken specifically. On menus both appear.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鳥皮|とりかわ}の{塩焼|しおや}き: salt-grilled chicken skin
- {鳥皮|とりかわ}をパリパリに{焼|や}く: to grill the skin until crisp
- {鳥皮|とりかわ}ポン{酢|ず}: chicken skin with ponzu

CULTURAL NOTE:
- Yakitori cuts are ordered by name at the counter, usually by the skewer and with a choice of {塩|しお} (salt) or タレ (sauce). {鳥皮|とりかわ} sits alongside もも (thigh), ねぎま (thigh and leek), and {砂肝|すなぎも} (gizzard) on a standard list.
